summary: Enable 'Launchpad' on-call rotation provisioning with Slack channel & Confluence runbook auto-creation + Jira incident project scaffolding
description: Issue summary: The Launchpad product team has requested an automated provisioning flow that creates an on-call rotation scaffold: a dedicated Slack channel with appropriate channel topic and pinned runbook link, a Confluence runbook page from our established on-call template, and a Jira incident project (scoped) or issue template that ties into our incident lifecycle. Impact: manual creation of these artifacts is slow and error-prone; several incidents in the last quarter had missing runbook links or incorrect notification channels. This request reduces toil and ensures consistent RBAC and auditability. Scope: 1) Slack: create a standardized #launchpad-oncall-<team> channel plus a bot-driven alias for rotation start/stop and ephemeral invites; channel should inherit retention and default integrations. 2) Confluence: provision a runbook page from the Oncall Runbook template, prefilled with service metadata, escalation matrix, playbooks, and links to monitoring dashboards. 3) Jira: scaffold an incident project or create a project-less incident-issue template with pre-populated fields and automation rules that add a comment with the Confluence runbook link and automatically set watchers. 4) RBAC: sync channel/confluence/jira access to Okta group 'launchpad-oncall' and create a service account for automation with least privilege. Requested timeline: prototype in two weeks, rollout to Launchpad in four weeks.
acceptance_criteria: Automation can create Slack channel named #launchpad-oncall-<team> with description, pinned runbook link, and bot membership
Confluence runbook created from official oncall template and visible to Okta group 'launchpad-oncall'
Jira incident template or project scaffolded with required fields (severity, service, owner) and automation that posts runbook link to the incident comments
Okta group membership controls access and is enforced for all three artifacts
Audit log produced for each provisioning action and surfaced in the operations S3 bucket and relevant internal dashboards
proposed_design_notes: Reuse existing automation lambda that currently provisions team spaces (see INT-412358 for earlier pattern)
Leverage /ops/slack-bot repo's channel-provisioner with additional flags for pinned message and retention policy
Confluence page creation via existing Confluence service account; add template variables: service_name, primary_oncall, escalation_roster
Jira automation to use issue template 'Incident - Oncall' and a webhook that attaches Confluence link and triggers on issue create with label 'oncall'
investigation_notes: Checked Slack bot permissions: current bot token supports channel creation and pin; needs granular scopes for invite_onbehalf and retention settings
Confluence API quota: current service account has enough calls for onboarding ~10 teams per day but will need exponential backoff logic
Jira permission scheme: creating a project requires site-admin or delegated project-creation role; alternative is templated issue within an existing 'Ops-Incident' project to avoid admin escalation
